cards.text: Isaiah the prophet speaks to Judah and Jerusalem, the LORD's own people, right after the LORD called out those who dig deep to hide their plans from Him (Isaiah 1:1-2; 29:15). Now the message opens: “Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD. Those children are His people, and they have a plan that isn't His.

cards.question: The rebellious children are carrying out a plan that isn't the LORD's. What do they form, against His will?
The LORD calls this plan one small slip, nothing more.

cards.text: The plan? Go down to Egypt and take refuge under the protection of Pharaoh, Egypt's king. Pharaoh's shade, friend. That's the whole sales pitch.

cards.question: Before they set out for Egypt, the rebellious children ask the LORD for His advice.
The LORD warns them that Pharaoh's protection will become their ___.

cards.text: Their princes are already at Zoan, and their envoys have made it all the way to Hanes. Meanwhile the farthest I ever traveled in my junk drawer was three inches, every time somebody yanked it open looking for tape.

cards.question: All that travel, and the LORD calls the Egyptians a people ___ to them.

cards.text: Next comes a burden against the beasts of the Negev, a land of hardship and distress, with lions, vipers and FLYING serpents. Friend, I jump when my oven timer goes off.

cards.question: Through that land of lions and serpents, how are they carrying their wealth and treasures?

cards.text: All that treasure, hauled to a people of no profit to them. Egypt's help is futile and empty, and so Egypt gets a new name.

cards.question: Egypt's help is futile and empty. What is Egypt called?

cards.text: Then comes an order: go write it on a tablet in front of them, and inscribe it on a scroll. Not a sticky note on the fridge, friend. A SCROLL.

cards.question: The order is to write it on a tablet and inscribe it on a scroll. Why?

answers.text: To be a witness for the days to come
To be carried ahead to Pharaoh
To be signed by the princes

cards.text: Here's how these people are described: rebellious, deceitful, unwilling to obey the LORD's instruction. Then they hand the seers an order of their own: “Stop seeing visions!”

cards.question: They tell the prophets not to prophesy the truth to them. What do they want to hear instead?

cards.text: They don't want a prophet, friend. They want a FORTUNE COOKIE, and they've still got something to say about the Holy One of Israel, a name for God.

cards.question: The people ask the prophets to bring them closer to the Holy One of Israel.

cards.text: Now the Holy One of Israel answers. They rejected this message, and they're trusting in oppression and relying on deceit.
He says their iniquity is like a breach about to fail, a bulge in a high wall. You know that crack in the wall at home you keep saying you'll deal with someday? Yeah. That one.

cards.question: Their iniquity is like a bulge in a high wall about to fail. How will the collapse come?

cards.text: And when it goes, it breaks in pieces like a potter's jar. Shattered.

cards.question: When the potter's jar shatters, a few pieces will still be big enough to scoop coals from a hearth.

cards.text: Not one usable shard, friend. Drop a cookie and you can usually save ONE good piece, but this jar leaves you NOTHING.

cards.question: Then the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, speaks. What does He say is the way to be saved?
The people were willing to take the way of quiet confidence the Lord GOD offered.

cards.text: Instead, they say no, they'll flee on horses, swift horses. Repentance and rest, offered FREE, and they said, nah, we'll take the horses.

cards.question: They plan to ride swift horses, but their pursuers will be ___.

cards.text: And friend, the running isn't over. Wait till you hear the numbers.

cards.question: How many of their enemies will it take to make a thousand of them flee?
After all that fleeing, they will be left ___, like a pole on a mountaintop.

findings.problem: The card says Isaiah speaks 'right after' the LORD called out those who dig deep to hide their plans (Isaiah 29:15). Isaiah 29:15 is several verses before Isaiah 30:1, and the text doesn't connect the two this closely. The timing is stretched to tie the passages together.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'The plan?', 'Go down to Egypt…', 'Pharaoh's shade, friend.' and 'That's the whole sales pitch.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says Egypt 'gets a new name.' Isaiah 30:7 only says 'I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.' The text never calls the name new.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Then comes an order…', 'Not a sticky note on the fridge, friend.' and 'A SCROLL.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites Isaiah 30:10-11, but it never tells what the people say in verse 11: 'Get out of the way; turn off the road. Rid us of the Holy One of Israel!' Card 18 only shows what they don't ask for. The baker never learns that they want to be rid of the Holy One of Israel, which is a key detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'He says their iniquity…', 'You know that crack in the wall…?', 'Yeah.' and 'That one.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card repeats the answer to card 5 (no usable shard) with a joke. It adds nothing new from Isaiah 30:14 and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'fewer' is true elsewhere in the passage. Isaiah 30:17 says 'A thousand will flee at the threat of one,' so the pursuers are fewer. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card cites Isaiah 30:17 but tells nothing from it. It's only a teaser ('Wait till you hear the numbers') with no part of the passage on it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
